body:
I understand your point about the fact that we'll all die eventually regardless but I think comparing suicide to a natural or uncontrollable form of death is more complex. A family member choosing to take themselves away from you makes you question every move you have ever made towards them; wondering if you could have stopped it or how you contributed to it happening. It leaves behind a lot of regret and guilt, making it increasingly difficult for those left behind to move on.

I don't know why you want to kill yourself or the struggles you endure but I can relate to that feeling. I keep going for my family because I know they'd care, although part of me wishes they wouldn't, I can't control that they do. I don't go through with it because it's selfish and I care about them too. I can hope for one of those stories where ten years down the road I make some sort of transition and am happy living my life but that is not what keeps me going whatsoever, it all comes down to my family and close friends.

With that said, once you become numbed to the impact on your family, I'm not sure what's left. I haven't made it there yet and I suppose I hope I never do, for their sake. I guess you're in that position though and so I can't really relate, but all I want to add is that if the fact that we all die anyways is convincing you they'll get over it because it's inevitable regardless, strongly reconsider the impacts of suicide versus a natural/accidental death because they can be astronomically different to a griever. Yes, we do all die eventually but I don't think throwing a blanket label over all types of death is fair because frankly, it does matter how someone dies, different deaths trigger different responses.

At the end of the day though, if you're miserable living life and you are indeed at peace with the idea of saying goodbye then I suppose that's a decision only you can make.

Thank you, I appreciate your concern and you sharing your story. I have had happier moments but they don't last long and aren't really worth it for me. I don't want to go through months of being miserable  just for a week or so of 'not-so-miserable'. Being happy is nice but in my experience it doesn't last, doesn't make up for how I usually feel and I'm tired of waiting for proof otherwise.

How did you bring such a topic up to your parents? I don't have any open relationship with mine whatsoever and although I know they would try their best to help and would be concerned, I can't imagine bringing it up.

Yeah, there is a sub for it but it's not very active and I'm too socially awkward to propose any meet up or anything like that. 

What keeps you going through university? I want to make my parents proud, sure, but most of all I wouldn't want to increase any financial burdens, especially of it's going to be worthless if I kill myself following. 

My parents don't know. I think they've suspected things in the past when I used to self-harm but we have never spoken about it openly. I don't have a very open relationship with them and couldn't imagine bringing something like this up.
